items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: I mentioned a Ronnie Milsap record – I did that twenty years ago but I still love the arrangements I wrote on Ronnie’s record. I only wrote six of the arrangements.

ctx.x: What possessed you – I’m wondering if there was an Aha! moment or – because I was looking at the Top 10 list of various years. And in the late ‘50s, early ‘60s there was such a variety of things. In 1949 you had “Bird with Strings” and then 1950 the “Third Man Theme,” and Nat King Cole, Roger Williams, “Rock Around the Clock.” Did some particular tune or style make a big impression on you?

That’s a good question because prior to me going and playing in the bar when I was 15, I remember over the summer I started to listen more closely to the radio. And I heard The Four Freshman sing “Day by Day.” And I went and I bought the record. And also I heard Johnny Ray sing “Cry” and “The Little White Cloud that Cried.” In fact I actually wrote an arrangement that I really, really liked for Ronnie Milsap with a big band and strings of the song “Cry” which actually became, for a while it was like a favorite,…

really reach. And as a result of it I didn’t realize that the true gift was not writing the notes on the paper, it was coming up with the idea. And for some reason instinctively I was gifted to come up with ideas. Like The Four Seasons – we needed an intro and there was scuffling. So I go to the piano on “Candy Girl” and I played this. I played four chords and I says, “How’s this?” They said, “What did you do?” And the take “Dawn (Go Away),” which was written as a folk song and make it sound like it was an…
